The ligament fibers are intact. No fiber disruption. Grade 2 MCL Injury: Partial disruption of ligament fibers. Increased signal within the ligament. Thickening and irregularity of the MCL. Periligamentous edema often more pronounced than in Grade I. May see a wavy or lax appearance of the ligament. Grade 3 MCL Injury: Complete disruption of MCL fibers. Ligament may be discontinuous or retracted.
